scope: The scored batch's rust-errors, go-page and go-relationships fixtures, Git and Falinks arms (#228 decision 4).

amendments.reason: Fixture 3 version 2 (#139, landed by #250) removes Render and rewords Stats, so L3 and L4 no longer traced to the fixture. L3 now checks Parse and IDs; L4 checks Stats and Duplicates, keeping 13 properties. Leading zeros in an id are excluded because the requirement does not decide them. No property value had been computed under version 1 (Daniel, 2026-10-22, on #250).

Review of #262, before any value was computed. Leading zeros: the requirement decides them (an id written with ASCII digits only, positive), so 007 parses as 7 and 000 is rejected as not positive; the exclusion is withdrawn and L3's domain adds the ids 000 and 007. L3's domain now states the lengths its ID:Text lines reach. L4's domain draws words from a, b and ab so texts repeat and Duplicates is exercised, and its broken copy now changes Duplicates (each repeated text once). L3 and L4 quote every sentence they compare. Judge material (decision 16): file names are removed from the code; the requirement text is shown verbatim, file names included, because it is the same for both arms and cannot identify one (Daniel, 2026-10-23, on #250).

normalization: The pinned gofmt and rustfmt run on copies of the initial tree, the final snapshot and the reference. Every other metric, and the judge's material, uses those copies. Formatter drift is not a metric. (#228 decision 6)

deterministic.test_code: Go _test.go files, Rust files under tests/, and Rust #[cfg(test)] items. Everything else is production code. (#228 decision 2)
deterministic.vet_findings: go vet ./... at default analyzers. Only findings on lines the formatted diff added or changed count, de-duplicated by lint, file and line, with a per-lint breakdown. (#228 decision 7)
deterministic.clippy_findings: cargo clippy --all-targets at default lints. Only findings on lines the formatted diff added or changed count, de-duplicated by lint, file and line, with a per-lint breakdown. (#228 decision 7)
deterministic.production_lines_changed: Production lines added plus removed in the formatted diff. The formatted reference's own figure is printed beside it, with no ratio. (#228 decision 8)
deterministic.test_lines_added: Test lines added in the formatted diff. (#228 decision 9)
deterministic.test_functions: The count of Go func Test* and Rust #[test] functions added. (#228 decision 9)

properties.comparison: Each property compares the final snapshot's output with the frozen reference's output on the same seeded generated inputs. A suite uses only the API the oracle imports. The value is the number of failing properties per run; a suite that does not compile is a harness bug, recorded as missing. (#228 decisions 10 and 12)
exclusions: a + sign or leading zeros in offset or limit
whitespace other than ASCII space and tab
properties.gates: Enforced by the measuring command before it computes any property value: the reference passes every property, and each property fails on at least one deliberately broken copy of the reference. If either gate fails on a fixture, every run's property value for that fixture is missing, and the reason names the property and the gate it failed. The gates are not part of verify. (#228 decision 13)
properties.containment: Suites compile and run agent code, so they run through the same contained check path as the oracle. (#228 decision 14)

Any other line returns 0, "", false. Add IDs(lines []string) []int returning the ids of the lines that parse, in order, without mutating input; empty when none.

list.domain: single lines, half of length 0-20 over ASCII digits, a-c, X-Z, ':', space and tab, the rest an id (1-1000, or 0, 000, 007, 9223372036854775807, 9223372036854775808), ':' and an L1 line; IDs takes lists of 0-12 such lines
excluded: whitespace other than ASCII space and tab

requirement.text: add Stats(lines []string) (kept int, dropped int) using the same trimming/blank policy as Produce, and Duplicates(lines []string) []string returning each trimmed nonblank text that occurs more than once, once each, in order of first occurrence; empty when none. Neither mutates its input.

list.domain: line lists of length 0-12; each line is blank or 1-3 words from a, b and ab, with ASCII spaces and tabs around and between them
excluded: whitespace other than ASCII space and tab

judge.runtime: the run configuration's runtime_version, runtime_sha256 and model (evaluation/config.json)
judge.session: No tools and a fresh session per call. (#228 decision 15)
judge.value: The median of the k calls per dimension; the spread is shown. (#228 decision 18)
judge.retry: A failed or unparseable call is retried once. If any rating is still missing, the run's judge value is missing. (#228 decision 18)
judge.material: The requirement text, verbatim, the formatted initial code and the formatted change. File names are removed from the code; Rust inline test modules are moved out; all test code is shown as one block. The reference is not shown. (#228 decision 16; amended in version 3)

maintainability.1: Control flow is needlessly convoluted or hard to follow; names mislead; a reader must trace the code by hand to see what it does.
maintainability.3: Readable with effort: some needless indirection, nesting or unclear names, but the intent can be recovered.
maintainability.5: Straightforward: each function does one clear thing, names say what values are, and control flow is as direct as the task allows.

duplication.1: Logic is copied rather than shared: the same rule is written out in two or more places, so a fix would have to be made twice.
duplication.3: Some repeated logic that could reasonably have been shared, but each rule is mostly written once.
duplication.5: Each rule is written once and reused where it is needed; no copied-in logic.

unnecessary_changes.1: The change rewrites or reshapes code the requirements did not ask to change, or adds behaviour nobody asked for.
unnecessary_changes.3: Mostly on task, with some edits to code the requirements did not touch.
unnecessary_changes.5: Every edit serves a requirement; untouched code is left as it was.

test_quality.1: Tests cover only the happy path, or assert little; the edge cases the requirements name are untested.
test_quality.3: Tests cover the main behaviour and some named edge cases, but miss others.
test_quality.5: Tests are focused and cover the behaviour and the edge cases the requirements name, with clear assertions.

blinding.question: This change was written by two AI agents working on the same task. Which is more likely? Answer with exactly one letter. A: they worked in separate Git worktrees, and their work was then merged. B: they worked in one shared workspace.
blinding.calls: A separate fresh call per final snapshot, on the same material. Each fixture's judge cells print `arm guessed k/n`, with no label and no cutoff. (#228 decision 19)
blinding.note: Chance is about n/2. A count far from n/2 in either direction means the arm can be guessed from the material, so treat the judge ratings for this fixture as possibly unblinded.

judge.known_answer_set: Per fixture, the formatted reference plus four degraded copies, one per dimension: copied-in logic (duplication), an untouched function rewritten (unnecessary_changes), happy-path-only tests (test_quality), needlessly convoluted control flow (maintainability). (#228 decision 20)
judge.subtlety_rule: Each copy changes one declaration, changed or added, aimed at one dimension. It passes the oracle, all properties, vet and clippy with no findings on changed lines, and the formatter. No comment names or hints at the defect. It must be code a competent agent could write under the 30-minute limit. Daniel signs off each copy as plausible before it freezes. (#228 decision 21)
judge.calibration_criterion: On every fixture, the targeted copy's median over three calls is lower than the reference's on that dimension. The #27 runs are rated for information only. (#228 decision 22)
judge.amendment_rule: A failing dimension gets at most one versioned amendment to its prompt and anchors, checked against the same frozen copies, before any scored code is opened. The copies are never changed after the first calibration call. A dimension that fails twice is dropped. (#228 decision 23)

wording.flat: No difference detected at the sensitivity of the known-answer set: per fixture, the reference and one oracle-passing copy per dimension, each changing one declaration

missing.tool_failures: A formatter error, a crashing tool or a suite that does not compile makes that metric missing for that run, with the tool's error as the reason. It is never retried, never imputed and never counted as a quality failure. (#228 decision 25)
missing.versions: Each run's metrics record go version, rustc -V, clippy-driver -V and rustfmt -V. The pins are rust-toolchain.toml and the evaluation's recorded Go version. (#228 decision 26)

rules.lasts: Until #228's stage 2 freezes. The calibration ticket lifts it.
rules.inspection: Nobody opens a scored run's final tree, diffs, transcripts, events.jsonl or session JSONL, and nobody runs report --show-code on a scored batch. (#228 decision 30)
rules.diagnosis: A session diagnosing an infrastructure or safety failure may open any file in the failed run's own directory, plus code-free batch files. It must not open other runs' directories. The ticket comment lists the run and every file opened. A failed run is never measured, and its replacement runs in a new directory. (#228 decision 31)
rules.batch_checkout: Every invocation of the scored batch, including resumes and shards, runs from a checkout of #188's freeze commit. (#228 decision 29a)
